children.text: Planetary Physics

Neglect planetary surface curvature and use \((1+x)^a\simeq1+ax\) for |x|≪1. Part A begins with two vertical plates of width w whose lower edges are h below the surrounding water surface. Oil of density ρoil<ρ0 is poured between the plates until its lower surface reaches their lower edges. Plates and vessel walls are tall enough to prevent overflow. Neglect mixing and surface tension. Next model the mid-ocean ridge in the figure as invariant along a length L in y. The crust is thin compared with its horizontal variation and behaves as a freely bendable plate. The mantle flows as an incompressible fluid. At x=0 crust thickness is zero. At infinity it is D and the sea bed has subsided by h. The origin is the ridge summit and z points downwards. Water density and temperature are ρ0,T0 and mantle values are ρ1,T1. Crustal length varies as \(\ell(T)=\ell_1[1-k_l(T_1-T)/(T_1-T_0)]\), with |kl|≪1. Thermal conductivity κ and specific heat c are constant.

Far from the ridge the temperature varies linearly across the crust from T0 to T1. Use hydrostatic mantle and water pressures to find D.

Find the leading-order horizontal force on the right half of the crust in terms of ρ0,ρ1,h,L,k,g. Treat the mantle pressure as hydrostatic and use the source's leading-order thin-crust model.

If the crust is thermally isolated from the rest of Earth, estimate the timescale for its upper and lower temperatures to approach one another. Assume independence from the two initial temperatures.

statement.text:
Planetary Physics
Neglect planetary surface curvature and use \((1+x)^a\simeq1+ax\) for |x|≪1. Part A begins with two vertical plates of width w whose lower edges are h below the surrounding water surface. Oil of density ρoil<ρ0 is poured between the plates until its lower surface reaches their lower edges. Plates and vessel walls are tall enough to prevent overflow. Neglect mixing and surface tension. Next model the mid-ocean ridge in the figure as invariant along a length L in y. The crust is thin compared with its horizontal variation and behaves as a freely bendable plate. The mantle flows as an incompressible fluid. At x=0 crust thickness is zero. At infinity it is D and the sea bed has subsided by h. The origin is the ridge summit and z points downwards. Water density and temperature are ρ0,T0 and mantle values are ρ1,T1. Crustal length varies as \(\ell(T)=\ell_1[1-k_l(T_1-T)/(T_1-T_0)]\), with |kl|≪1. Thermal conductivity κ and specific heat c are constant.

a.1. Oil force on a plate
Find the signed horizontal net force on the right plate, taking rightwards as positive.
a.2. Thermal density law

Find the exact isotropic density law and its first-order form \(\rho(T)\simeq\rho_1[1+k(T_1-T)/(T_1-T_0)]\). Identify k.
a.3. Asymptotic crust thickness
Far from the ridge the temperature varies linearly across the crust from T0 to T1. Use hydrostatic mantle and water pressures to find D.
a.4. Horizontal force on the crust
Find the leading-order horizontal force on the right half of the crust in terms of ρ0,ρ1,h,L,k,g. Treat the mantle pressure as hydrostatic and use the source's leading-order thin-crust model.
a.5. Thermal relaxation time

b.1. Returning seismic ray

A line source at x=z=0 emits a ray at angle 0<θ0<π/2 from the downward vertical into a medium of speed v(z)=v0(1+z/z0). Its path is a circle arc. Find its next surface coordinate x1=A cot(bθ0), determining A,b.
b.2. Absorbed seismic energy density
The source releases energy E per unit length uniformly into the downward half-plane. Waves are absorbed on their first return to the surface. Find and sketch ε(x), energy per surface area.
b.3. Furthest shadow zone
Now reflect waves perfectly at the surface. Emit only the small angular interval θ0±δθ0/2, with δθ0≪θ0 and ≪1. To leading order find the furthest surface distance that is not reached by this signal.

children.text: Planetary Physics
a.1. Oil force on a plate

Bottom pressure matching gives oil column height \(h_o=\rho_0h/\rho_{oil}\). Integrating triangular pressure distributions on both sides yields \[F_x=\frac{\rho_0gh^2w}{2}\left(\frac{\rho_0}{\rho_{oil}}-1\right)>0.\]
a.2. Thermal density law
Each dimension changes by the same factor, so \[\rho(T)=\rho_1[1-k_l(T_1-T)/(T_1-T_0)]^{-3}\simeq\rho_1[1+3k_l(T_1-T)/(T_1-T_0)].\] Thus k=3kl.
a.3. Asymptotic crust thickness
The same mantle depth has equal pressure on the ridge axis and at infinity: \(\rho_1(h+D)=\rho_0h+\rho_1D(1+k/2)\). Therefore \[D=\frac{2h}{k}(1-\rho_0/\rho_1).\]
a.4. Horizontal force on the crust

Integrating the pressure tractions on the sloping upper and lower surfaces gives the difference of their projected vertical integrals. With common pressure pO at z=0, \[F=L\int_0^{h+D}(p_O+\rho_1gz)dz-L\int_0^h(p_O+\rho_0gz)dz.\] Thus \(F=Lp_OD+L\rho_1g(h+D)^2/2-L\rho_0gh^2/2\). Since D∝1/k and pO and h are fixed, the leading term is \[F\simeq\frac{2gLh^2(\rho_1-\rho_0)^2}{k^2\rho_1},\] directed away from the ridge. This is the force from the exterior fluids on the specified crust region.
a.5. Thermal relaxation time

The heat per area to redistribute is of order ρ1cDΔT, and conductive flux is of order κΔT/D. Their ratio gives \(\tau\sim\rho_1cD^2/\kappa\). Dimensional analysis determines the same scaling, with an undetermined order-one prefactor. The temperature difference cancels.
b.1. Returning seismic ray

Snell's law gives \(\sin\theta/(1+z/z_0)=\sin\theta_0\). The circle radius is \(R=z_0/\sin\theta_0\), with centre at depth −z0. Its surface chord is \(x_1=2R\cos\theta_0=2z_0\cot\theta_0\). Thus A=2z0,b=1.
b.2. Absorbed seismic energy density

An angular interval dθ carries E dθ/π. Since \(|dx/d\theta|=2z_0\csc^2\theta\), \[\epsilon(x)=\frac{2Ez_0}{\pi(4z_0^2+x^2)}.\] The plot is even, peaks at E/(2πz0) at the origin, decays as 1/x², and integrates to E over the entire surface.
b.3. Furthest shadow zone

The nth return illuminates an interval centred at n x1 with width n|x1′|δθ0. Adjacent intervals first overlap when \(n\sim x_1/(|x_1^{\prime}|\delta\theta_0)\). Thus the last gap lies near \[x_{max}\simeq\frac{x_1^2}{|x_1^{\prime}|\delta\theta_0}=\frac{2z_0\cos^2\theta_0}{\delta\theta_0}.\] This is a leading narrow-beam estimate, with discrete-reflection corrections.
